title: Cooked basmati rice
description: Fluffy, separate grains for the week. Cook a big pot and use it by weight in curd rice, lemon rice, fried rice and bowls.
notes: 300 g of raw rice makes about 900 g cooked.
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swirling and draining, until the water runs almost clear (three or four changes). Soak it for 15 minutes if you have time, then drain.
Bring the water and salt to a boil in a pot with a tight lid. Add the rice, stir once, and bring back to a boil.
Turn the heat to the lowest setting, cover and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 5 more minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Spread it on a tray to cool quickly, then keep it in a covered box in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Cooked jasmine rice
description: Soft, fragrant rice for curries and stir fries. Day-old rice from the fridge makes the best fried rice.
steps: Rinse the rice two or three times until the water is only a little cloudy, then drain well.
Put the rice and water in a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 13 minutes. Rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff it up. Cool what you won't eat now on a tray, then refrigerate it in a covered box for up to 4 days.

title: Cooked brown rice
description: Nutty, chewy brown rice cooked like pasta, so it never goes gluey. Freezes well in portions.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the salt.
Rinse the rice, add it to the pot and boil uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Drain it in a sieve, put it back in the empty pot, cover and leave it off the heat for 10 minutes to steam.
Fluff and cool. Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer.

title: Ginger-garlic paste
description: The base of most Indian curries. A jar in the fridge saves peeling and chopping every night.
ingredients: 100 g | fresh ginger | peeled and roughly chopped
steps: Put the ginger, garlic, oil and salt in a small blender or food processor.
Blend to a smooth paste, scraping down the sides a few times. Add a spoon of water only if it won't turn.
Pack it into a clean jar and smooth the top. It keeps 2 weeks in the fridge; freeze spoonfuls in an ice cube tray for longer.

title: Quick pickled onions
description: Bright pink, sharp and crunchy. They lift tacos, bowls, salads and sandwiches, and they're ready in half an hour.
steps: Pack the sliced onions into a clean jar.
Warm the vinegar, water, sugar and salt in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. It only needs to be warm, not boiling.
Pour it over the onions, pressing them down so they're covered.
Leave for 30 minutes at room temperature, then close the jar and refrigerate. They keep for 2 weeks.

title: Cooked chickpeas
description: Cheaper and creamier than canned. Cook a batch from dry for chana masala, hummus, salads and sundal.
notes: 500 g dried makes about 1.1 kg cooked.
steps: Drain the soaked chickpeas and rinse them.
Put them in a big pot with the water and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Simmer, partly covered, for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until they're tender all the way through. Add the salt for the last 15 minutes. (In a pressure cooker: 15 minutes at pressure.)
Cool them in their liquid, then keep them in a box with a little of it. 5 days in the fridge, or freeze in portions.

title: Meal-prep chicken breast
description: Juicy baked chicken breast to slice into salads, wraps, rice bowls and sandwiches all week.
notes: Chicken loses about a quarter of its weight as it cooks: 1 kg raw is about 750 g cooked.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C. If the breasts are thick at one end, pound them to an even thickness between two sheets of baking paper.
Rub them with the oil, then the salt, paprika, garlic powder and pepper.
Lay them on a lined tray, not touching, and bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 74 °C.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Onion-tomato masala base
description: A slow-cooked onion, tomato and spice base. Freeze it in portions, and a weeknight curry is fifteen minutes away.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden brown. Take your time: this is where the flavour comes from.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and chilies and cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Cook for about 10 minutes, mashing them, until they fall apart.
Add the turmeric, chili powder and coriander and cook for 5 more minutes, until the oil separates at the edges.
Cool and freeze in portions of about 150 g, enough for a curry for two.

title: Hard-boiled eggs
description: Peelable, set yolks, no grey ring. A dozen in the fridge covers breakfasts, salads and snacks.
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot.
Lower the eggs in gently with a spoon and boil for 10 minutes (8 for a softer, jammy yolk).
Move them straight into a bowl of ice water and leave for 5 minutes.
Keep them in their shells in the fridge for up to a week; peel as you need them.

title: Lemon vinaigrette
description: A jar of everyday dressing: lemon, olive oil, mustard and a little honey.
steps: Put everything in a jar with a lid.
Shake hard until it's thick and creamy.
Keep it in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. The oil sets when cold: leave it out for 10 minutes and shake again.

title: Sambar
description: Tangy lentil and vegetable stew with tamarind and sambar powder: the everyday comfort of Tamil homes, with rice, idli or dosa.
ingredients: 150 g | green beans | cut in 3 cm pieces
steps: Pressure cook the dal with the water and turmeric for 4 whistles (or simmer in a pot for 40 minutes) until completely soft. Mash it well.
In a big pot, simmer the onion, tomatoes, carrots, beans and eggplant in the second lot of water with the salt for 10 minutes, until nearly tender.
Stir in the tamarind and sambar powder and simmer for 5 minutes, until the raw smell of the tamarind is gone.
Add the mashed dal and simmer for 5 more minutes. Loosen with hot water if it's thicker than a pouring soup.
For the tempering, heat the ghee in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the asafetida, chilies and curry leaves. Pour it over the sambar.
Finish with cilantro. It tastes even better the next day.

title: Tomato rasam
description: A thin, peppery tomato and tamarind broth. Drink it from a cup, or mix it into hot rice with a spoon of ghee when you're under the weather.
steps: Squeeze the tomatoes with your hands into a pot, then add the tamarind, rasam powder, garlic, pepper, cumin, turmeric, salt and water.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down.
Turn the heat right down. Rasam should froth up but never boil hard once it's ready, or it turns bitter.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaves and chili. Pour into the rasam.
Add the cilantro, cover and let it sit for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Curd rice (thayir sadam)
description: Cool, creamy rice with yogurt and a crackling mustard seed tempering. The calm end to a South Indian meal, and perfect for a hot day.
steps: Mash the rice lightly with the back of a spoon while it's still a little warm (warm the fridge rice briefly if needed). Let it cool.
Stir in the yogurt, milk and salt. It should be soft and loose; it thickens as it stands.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Add the mustard seeds and, when they pop, the urad dal. Stir until the dal is golden, then add the chili, ginger, curry leaves and asafetida for a few seconds.
Pour the tempering over the rice and mix in the cucumber and cilantro.
Top with pomegranate. Serve cool, with pickle on the side. Add a splash of milk if it firms up in the fridge.

title: Chettinad chicken curry
description: A dark, fiery curry from Chettinad, built on freshly roasted spices, black pepper and coconut.
ingredients: 800 g | chicken thighs | boneless, cut in chunks
steps: Dry-roast the coriander, cumin, fennel, peppercorns, chilies, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant. Add the coconut and keep stirring until it's golden.
Cool, then grind to a fine paste with a few spoons of water.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Fry the curry leaves for a few seconds, then add the onions and cook until golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, then the tomatoes and turmeric, and cook until the tomatoes are soft.
Add the chicken and salt and stir for 5 minutes to coat and colour the pieces.
Stir in the spice paste and water. Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick and clinging.
Finish with cilantro. Serve with rice, parotta or dosa.

title: Lemon rice
description: Turmeric-yellow rice with lemon, peanuts and curry leaves. A lunchbox classic that's good at room temperature.
steps: Spread the rice out so the grains are separate and cool.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the chana dal, urad dal and peanuts and stir until golden.
Add the chilies, ginger, curry leaves and asafetida, then the turmeric, and turn off the heat straight away.
Add the rice and salt and toss gently until every grain is yellow.
Sprinkle over the lemon juice and cilantro and toss again. Taste for salt and lemon.

title: Tamarind rice (puliyodarai)
description: Temple-style rice tossed with a thick, sweet-sour tamarind paste, sesame and peanuts. It travels well and tastes better the next day.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds, coriander seeds, fenugreek and pepper in a dry pan until the sesame is golden. Cool and grind to a powder.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan. Pop the mustard seeds, then fry the chana dal, urad dal and peanuts until golden. Add the chilies, curry leaves, asafetida and turmeric.
Pour in the tamarind, water, jaggery and salt. Simmer, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens to a glossy paste and the oil rises.
Stir in half of the spice powder.
Mix the paste into the cooled rice with the rest of the powder. Leave it for 30 minutes so the rice soaks up the flavour.

title: Cabbage poriyal
description: Finely shredded cabbage stir-fried with mustard seeds, curry leaves and fresh coconut. A light, crunchy side for sambar and rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan. Add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the urad dal, red chili, curry leaves and green chili.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage, turmeric and salt. Stir-fry over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes. Keep a little crunch; don't add water.
Turn off the heat, stir in the coconut and serve.

title: Green beans poriyal
description: Finely chopped green beans with coconut and a mustard seed tempering, the way it's served at weddings in Tamil Nadu.
steps: Cook the beans with the water and salt in a covered pan for 6 to 8 minutes, until just tender. Uncover and let any water left cook off.
In another pan, heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds. Add the urad dal and fry until golden, then the chili, curry leaves and asafetida.
Tip in the beans and toss for a minute.
Turn off the heat and mix in the coconut.

title: Beetroot poriyal
description: Sweet, jewel-bright beetroot cooked with green chili and coconut. Even people who don't like beets tend to like this.
ingredients: 450 g | beetroot | peeled and finely diced
steps: Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then fry the chana dal until golden. Add the curry leaves, chili and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the beetroot, salt and water. Cover and cook over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Cook uncovered for a minute to dry it out, then stir in the coconut.

title: Mixed vegetable kootu
description: A gentle, thick stew of moong dal and vegetables in a coconut-cumin paste. Mild enough for everyone, filling enough for a light meal.
steps: Cook the moong dal with the water and turmeric for 15 minutes until soft (or 2 whistles in a pressure cooker).
Add the pumpkin, beans, carrot and salt, with a splash more water if needed, and simmer for 10 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Grind the coconut, cumin and chilies with the water to a smooth paste. Stir it in and simmer for 5 minutes. It should be thick but spoonable.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, fry the urad dal until golden, add the curry leaves and pour it over the kootu.

title: Coconut chutney
description: The white chutney served with every idli and dosa: fresh coconut, roasted gram, green chili and a crackle of mustard seeds.
notes: Frozen grated coconut works well; thaw it first.
steps: Blend the coconut, roasted chana dal, chilies, ginger and salt with the water until smooth. Add a little more water for a pourable chutney.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, fry the urad dal until golden and add the curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the chutney. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Tomato onion chutney
description: A spicy red chutney for dosa, idli and uttapam, and a great sandwich spread too. It keeps for days.
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil and fry the urad dal and chilies until the dal is golden. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tamarind and salt and cook for 10 minutes until soft and jammy. Cool, then blend smooth.
Heat the rest of the oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the curry leaves and pour over the chutney.

title: Rava upma
description: A soft, savoury semolina porridge with vegetables and cashews, ready faster than you can get a delivery.
steps: Dry-roast the semolina in a pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it smells toasty but is still pale. Tip it onto a plate.
Heat the ghee in the same pan. Pop the mustard seeds, then fry the urad dal, chana dal and cashews until golden.
Add the onion, chili, ginger and curry leaves and cook for 3 minutes, then the carrot and peas for 2 more.
Pour in the water and salt and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low and add the semolina in a slow stream, stirring all the time so no lumps form. Cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Fluff it with a fork, add the lemon juice and cilantro, and serve hot with coconut chutney.

title: Ven pongal
description: Rice and moong dal cooked soft and creamy, with ghee, black pepper, cumin and ginger. The South Indian answer to a warm bowl of porridge.
steps: Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan for 2 minutes until fragrant. Rinse it with the rice.
Cook the rice and dal with the water and salt until very soft and mushy: 5 whistles in a pressure cooker, or 30 minutes in a covered pot, stirring now and then. Mash lightly.
Heat the ghee and fry the cashews until golden. Add the pepper, cumin, ginger, curry leaves and asafetida and fry for a few seconds.
Pour it all over the pongal and stir. Add hot water if it's stiff: it should be soft and spoonable. Serve with sambar and coconut chutney.

title: Kerala egg roast
description: Hard-boiled eggs in a thick, peppery onion masala cooked in coconut oil. Serve with appam, parotta or rice.
steps: Make shallow cuts in the eggs so the masala can get in.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds and add the curry leaves. Add the onions and chilies with a pinch of salt and cook for 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes until they melt.
Stir in the turmeric, chili powder, coriander, pepper and salt and cook for 2 minutes. Add the water.
Add the eggs, coat them in the masala and cook for 5 minutes until thick. Sprinkle over the garam masala.

title: Kerala fish curry
description: White fish simmered in coconut milk with tamarind, curry leaves and chili. Tangy, rich and ready in well under an hour.
ingredients: 600 g | white fish fillets | cut in large pieces
steps: Rub the fish with the turmeric and half a teaspoon of salt and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Pop the mustard seeds, then add the fenugreek and curry leaves for a few seconds.
Add the onion, ginger, garlic and chilies and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the tomato and cook until it breaks down.
Stir in the chili powder and coriander for a minute, then the tamarind, water and salt. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Slide in the fish and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, shaking the pan rather than stirring so the fish stays whole.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving with rice.

title: Pepper chicken fry
description: Dry, glossy chicken with a big hit of freshly crushed black pepper, fennel and curry leaves.
ingredients: 750 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in bite-size pieces
steps: Mix the chicken with the ginger-garlic paste, turmeric and salt and leave it for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan. Add the fennel and curry leaves, then the onions and chilies, and cook until golden.
Add the chicken and cook over high heat for 5 minutes to brown, then cover and cook on medium for 10 minutes, until cooked through.
Uncover, add the pepper and coriander and stir-fry for 5 more minutes until dry and dark.
Finish with the lemon juice.

title: Chicken 65
description: Chennai's famous fried chicken bites: marinated in chili, ginger and garlic, fried crisp and tossed with curry leaves.
ingredients: 600 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in bite-size pieces
60 g | neutral oil | absorbed from about 1 l for deep frying
steps: Mix everything in the marinade except the cornstarch and rice flour. Leave for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Stir in the cornstarch and rice flour so each piece has a thick coat.
Heat the oil for deep frying to 175 °C. Fry the chicken in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until deep red, crisp and cooked through. Drain on paper.
In a wok, heat a tablespoon of oil and fry the curry leaves, chilies and garlic for 30 seconds. Toss in the chicken and serve straight away with onion rings and lemon.

title: Avial
description: A Kerala medley of vegetables in a coconut, cumin and yogurt sauce, finished with raw coconut oil and curry leaves.
ingredients: 150 g | green beans | cut in batons
steps: Put the vegetables in a pan with the turmeric, salt and water. Cover and cook gently for 10 to 12 minutes until just tender, not mushy.
Grind the coconut, cumin and chilies to a coarse paste with the water.
Stir the paste into the vegetables and cook for 3 minutes.
Take it off the heat and fold in the yogurt.
Drizzle over the coconut oil, scatter the curry leaves on top and cover for 5 minutes so their aroma soaks in.

title: Spinach dal (keerai kootu)
description: Spinach and moong dal cooked down with garlic and cumin, then mashed smooth. Iron-rich and gentle, with plain rice and a spoon of ghee.
steps: Cook the dal with the water and turmeric until soft, about 15 minutes.
Add the spinach, onion, tomato, chilies, garlic and salt and cook for 8 minutes until the spinach collapses.
Mash with a potato masher or a few pulses of a stick blender. Keep some texture.
Heat the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, add the cumin, chilies and asafetida and pour it over.

title: Chickpea sundal
description: Warm chickpeas tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves, coconut and lemon. The beach snack of Chennai, and a protein-packed one.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan. Pop the mustard seeds, then fry the urad dal until golden and add the chilies, curry leaves, asafetida and ginger.
Add the chickpeas and salt and toss for 3 minutes until hot.
Turn off the heat and mix in the coconut, lemon juice and cilantro.

title: Rava kesari
description: A glossy, saffron-orange semolina pudding with ghee, cardamom, cashews and raisins. Festival food in twenty minutes.
steps: Warm a tablespoon of the ghee and fry the cashews and raisins until the cashews are golden. Lift them out.
Add the semolina to the pan with another tablespoon of ghee and roast over low heat for 5 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Meanwhile bring the water to a boil with the saffron.
Pour the water into the semolina slowly, stirring hard (it will splutter). Cook until it's absorbed, about 2 minutes.
Add the sugar: it melts and loosens the mix. Keep stirring and add the rest of the ghee a little at a time until the kesari leaves the sides of the pan.
Stir in the cardamom, cashews and raisins. Serve warm.

title: Spiced buttermilk (neer mor)
description: Thin, salty, cooling yogurt drink with ginger, green chili and curry leaves: the best thing on a hot afternoon.
steps: Whisk the yogurt with the cold water until smooth.
Stir in the ginger, chili, curry leaves, cilantro, salt and asafetida.
Leave for 10 minutes in the fridge for the flavours to come through, then serve cold.

title: South Indian filter coffee
description: Strong decoction, frothy hot milk and sugar, poured back and forth between tumbler and davara until foamy.
notes: Nutrition counts the brewed coffee only; the grounds stay in the filter.
ingredients: 20 g | coffee | ground, with chicory if you like
steps: Put the coffee in the top of a South Indian filter (or a French press) and press it down lightly.
Pour over the boiling water, cover and let it drip for 15 minutes to make a thick decoction.
Heat the milk until it's just boiling.
For each cup, put a teaspoon of sugar and about 50 ml of decoction in a tumbler and top up with milk.
Pour it between the tumbler and a bowl from a height a few times, until it's frothy.

title: Chicken dum biryani
description: Spiced yogurt-marinated chicken layered with long-grain basmati, fried onions, mint and saffron, then sealed and steamed. A weekend project that feeds a crowd.
ingredients: 1 kg | chicken thighs | bone-in or boneless, in large pieces
a pinch | saffron | soaked in 60 ml warm milk
steps: Mix the chicken with everything in the marinade and leave it for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat, stirring, for 15 to 20 minutes until deep brown and crisp. Lift out half for the top; mix the rest, and the oil, into the chicken.
Spread the chicken in a heavy, wide pot with a tight lid.
Bring the water to a rolling boil with the salt, bay leaves and whole spices. Add the drained rice and boil for 5 to 6 minutes, until it's about 70% cooked: it should still snap in the middle.
Drain the rice and spread it over the chicken. Scatter over the reserved onions, drizzle with the ghee and the saffron milk.
Cover tightly (seal the lid with foil if it isn't snug). Cook on high heat for 5 minutes, then on the lowest heat for 35 minutes. Or bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, then dig down to the bottom with a big spoon so each plate gets rice and chicken. Serve with raita.

title: Dal tadka
description: Yellow lentils simmered soft, then finished with a sizzling tempering of ghee, cumin, garlic and chili. Dhaba-style comfort.
steps: Cook the dal with the water, turmeric and salt until completely soft: 4 whistles in a pressure cooker, or about 35 minutes in a pot. Whisk it smooth.
Heat the ghee, sizzle the cumin, then cook the onion until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and green chili and cook until soft. Stir in the chili powder, coriander and garam masala.
Tip the masala into the dal and simmer for 5 minutes. Add hot water to get the consistency you like.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan until very hot. Add the garlic and fry until golden, then the red chilies and asafetida. Pour it over the dal right away, so it sizzles.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with rice or roti.

title: Chana masala
description: Chickpeas in a dark, tangy onion-tomato gravy with amchur-sour notes from lemon. Even better the next day, with rice, bhature or bread.
steps: Heat the oil, add the cumin and bay leaf, then the onions. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until well browned.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilies and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook until thick and the oil separates, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, chili powder, coriander and cumin for a minute.
Add the chickpeas, water and salt. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice. Top with ginger and cilantro.

title: Palak paneer
description: Soft cubes of paneer in a vivid green, gently spiced spinach sauce. Blanching the spinach quickly keeps the colour bright.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then plunge it into ice water. Blend with the green chilies and a splash of the water to a smooth puree.
Heat the ghee and sizzle the cumin. Cook the onion until soft and golden, then the ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then the tomato until it melts.
Add the coriander, garam masala and salt, then the spinach puree. Simmer for 5 minutes; don't cook it longer or it turns dull.
Add the paneer and simmer for 3 minutes. Stir in the cream and crumble in the kasoori methi.

title: Butter chicken
description: Charred, yogurt-marinated chicken in a silky, mildly spiced tomato, butter and cream sauce. Worth the two steps.
ingredients: 700 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in chunks
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala, salt and lemon. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the grill or broiler to high. Spread the chicken on an oiled tray and grill for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges.

For the sauce, melt the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cashews for a minute, then the tomatoes, chili powder, garam masala, sugar, salt and water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend the sauce until very smooth, then pour it back into the pan (strain it for a restaurant finish).
Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the cream and crushed kasoori methi. Serve with naan or rice.

title: Rajma (red kidney bean curry)
description: Kidney beans in a thick, homely gravy with onion, tomato and warm spices. Rajma chawal is Punjab's Sunday lunch.
ingredients: 2 cans | kidney beans | drained and rinsed
steps: Heat the oil, sizzle the cumin, and brown the onions well, about 12 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes. Cook until thick and the oil separates.
Add the turmeric, chili powder and coriander for a minute.
Add the beans, water and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, mashing some of the beans to make the gravy creamy.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro. Serve over rice.

title: Aloo gobi
description: Potatoes and cauliflower cooked dry with cumin, turmeric and ginger until golden at the edges.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan with a lid. Sizzle the cumin, then add the onion, ginger and chilies and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until they start to colour.
Add the cauliflower, turmeric, chili powder, coriander and salt. Toss well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender. Uncover for the last few minutes to crisp up.
Finish with garam masala and cilantro.

title: Jeera rice
description: Basmati rice cooked with ghee and toasted cumin seeds: the simple rice that goes with every dal and curry.
ingredients: 250 g | basmati rice | rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
steps: Heat the ghee in a pot. Add the cumin, bay leaf and cardamom and let the cumin darken a shade.
Add the drained rice and stir gently for a minute to coat the grains.
Add the water and salt and bring to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

title: Paneer bhurji
description: Crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and spices. A fast, high-protein breakfast or dinner, rolled in a roti.
steps: Heat the ghee, sizzle the cumin, and cook the onion, chili and ginger for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and spices and cook until the tomato is mushy.
Add the paneer and milk and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until hot. Don't overcook or the paneer gets rubbery.
Finish with cilantro. Serve with toast or roti.

title: Chicken tikka
description: Chunks of chicken in a tangy, spiced yogurt marinade, charred under a hot grill or on the barbecue. Great for meal prep bowls and wraps.
ingredients: 800 g | chicken breasts | in large chunks
steps: Mix everything except the onion and pepper into a thick marinade, add the chicken and coat well. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Thread the chicken, onion and pepper onto skewers, or spread them on a lined tray.
Grill under a very hot broiler (or on a barbecue) for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Serve with mint chutney, lemon and sliced onions.

title: Egg bhurji
description: Masala scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and green chili, the street-stall breakfast of Mumbai.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion and chili for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and spices and cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly over medium-low heat until softly set.
Take it off the heat while still a little wet (it keeps cooking) and add the cilantro. Serve with buttered toast or pav.

title: Red lentil dal (masoor dal)
description: Red lentils cook down to a golden, creamy dal in twenty minutes with no soaking. The fastest proper dinner there is.
steps: Simmer the lentils with the water, turmeric and salt for 20 minutes, skimming any foam, until they collapse. Whisk to a smooth soup.
Meanwhile heat the oil, sizzle the cumin, then cook the onion, garlic and ginger until golden. Add the tomato and chili powder and cook until soft.
Stir the tempering into the dal and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve with rice or bread.

title: Keema matar
description: Spiced minced meat with green peas: a quick weeknight curry that freezes brilliantly. Made here with lean beef; lamb is traditional.
steps: Heat the oil, sizzle the cumin, and brown the onions for 10 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilies for a minute, then the mince. Break it up and cook until it's no longer pink.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chili, coriander, cumin and salt. Cook for 10 minutes until the tomatoes collapse and the oil separates.
Add the peas and water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro. Serve with roti, pav or rice.

title: Aloo paratha
description: Whole wheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato and cooked on a hot griddle with a little ghee. Serve with yogurt and pickle.
steps: Mix the flour and salt, then add the water gradually and knead for 5 minutes to a soft dough. Rub with the oil, cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix all the filling ingredients. Make sure there are no lumps; they tear the paratha.
Divide the dough and filling into 6 each. Flatten a ball of dough into a 10 cm round, put a ball of filling in the middle and pull the edges up to seal it.
Flatten gently, dust with flour and roll out to about 18 cm, lightly so the filling doesn't burst out.
Cook on a hot griddle for a minute each side, then brush with ghee and press with a spatula until golden and puffed in places. Keep warm in a cloth while you cook the rest.

title: Rice kheer
description: Rice slowly simmered in milk until creamy, scented with cardamom and saffron and scattered with pistachios.
ingredients: 60 g | basmati rice | rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
steps: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pot. Add the drained rice.
Simmer on low heat for 40 to 45 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced by about a third.
Stir in the sugar, cardamom, saffron and almonds and cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve warm, or chill it: it thickens as it cools. Top with pistachios.

title: Mango lassi
description: Ripe mango blended with yogurt and a little cardamom. Canned Alphonso pulp is the secret outside mango season.
ingredients: 250 g | mango | ripe, peeled, or canned pulp
a pinch | cardamom pods | seeds ground
steps: Blend everything until smooth and frothy.
Taste and add more sugar if your mango isn't very sweet. Serve cold.

title: Masala chai
description: Milky black tea boiled with ginger, cardamom and a little clove and cinnamon. Adjust the sugar and spice to taste.
steps: Bring the water to a boil with the ginger, cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the tea leaves and boil for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk and sugar and bring back to a boil. Let it rise up the pan twice, lowering the heat each time.
Strain into cups.

title: Kanda poha
description: Flattened rice with onions, peanuts, turmeric and lemon: Maharashtra's light, quick breakfast.
steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve under running water for 20 seconds, just until soft. Drain and leave it for 5 minutes, then mix in the salt and sugar.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, and fry the peanuts until golden. Add the curry leaves, chilies and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the turmeric, then the poha, and toss gently over low heat for 3 minutes until hot and yellow.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro.

title: Besan chilla
description: Savoury chickpea-flour pancakes with onion, tomato and chili. Naturally gluten free and quick to whisk up.
steps: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water to a smooth batter, like thin pancake batter. Rest for 10 minutes.
Stir in the vegetables, herbs, spices and salt.
Heat a non-stick pan and brush with oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it into a thin round.
Cook for 2 minutes until the edges lift, drizzle a little oil around, flip and cook for another minute. Serve with green chutney or yogurt.

title: Cucumber raita
description: Cool yogurt with grated cucumber, mint and toasted cumin, to go with biryani and anything spicy.
ingredients: 1 tsp | cumin seeds | toasted and crushed
steps: Whisk the yogurt until smooth.
Stir in the cucumber, mint, cumin and salt.
Dust with chili powder and chill until needed.

title: Onion bhaji
description: Crisp, lacy fritters of sliced onion in a spiced chickpea-flour batter. Best eaten hot, with a cup of chai when it rains.
ingredients: 50 g | neutral oil | absorbed from about 1 l for deep frying
steps: Toss the onions with the salt and leave for 10 minutes: they'll release water.
Add the flours, chili, spices and cilantro and mix with your hands. Add water a spoon at a time only until the batter just coats the onions.
Heat the oil to 175 °C. Drop in loose clumps of the mix and fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve hot with chutney.

title: Egg fried rice
description: Day-old rice, eggs, scallions and soy sauce over the highest heat you've got. The fridge-clearing dinner.
ingredients: 3 | eggs | beaten with a pinch of salt
4 | scallions | sliced, whites and greens apart
steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your hands.
Heat a wok or large pan until smoking. Add half the oil, then the eggs; scramble them softly and tip them out while still a little wet.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and scallion whites and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the rice and peas and toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing the rice against the pan so it toasts.
Add the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, the white pepper and the eggs. Toss, then finish with sesame oil and scallion greens.

title: Chicken fried rice
description: A takeaway favourite, lighter and faster at home: chicken, egg, vegetables and rice with soy and oyster sauce.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and a tablespoon of soy sauce.
Heat a wok until very hot with a tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry the chicken for 4 minutes until cooked, then lift it out.
Scramble the eggs in the wok and lift them out.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, carrot and peas and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the rice and toss for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and egg, add the oyster sauce and soy sauce, and toss until everything is hot and evenly coloured. Finish with sesame oil and scallions.

title: Beef and broccoli
description: Tender strips of beef and crisp broccoli in a glossy garlic, soy and oyster sauce. Faster than delivery.
ingredients: 500 g | flank, skirt, or flatiron steak | thinly sliced across the grain
steps: Mix the beef with the soy sauce, cornstarch and baking soda and leave for 15 minutes. The baking soda keeps it tender.
Stir together the sauce ingredients.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat a wok until smoking with a tablespoon of oil. Sear the beef in one layer for a minute each side, in two batches, and lift out.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then the broccoli. Pour in the sauce and bubble until thick.
Return the beef, toss, and finish with sesame oil. Serve with rice.

title: Kung pao chicken
description: Sichuan stir fry of chicken, peanuts and dried chilies in a sweet, sour, tingly sauce.
ingredients: 500 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in 2 cm cubes
8 | dried red chilies | halved, seeds shaken out
steps: Marinate the chicken with the soy sauce, wine and cornstarch for 10 minutes. Mix the sauce ingredients.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat. Fry the chilies and peppercorns for 30 seconds until fragrant and darkening, but not black.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked.
Add the garlic, ginger and scallions for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy, then add the peanuts. Serve with rice.

title: Mapo tofu
description: Silky tofu in a fiery, numbing sauce with a little minced pork. Serve with lots of rice.
ingredients: 450 g | tofu | soft or medium, in 2 cm cubes
1 tbsp | chili oil w/ fermented soybeans
1 tbsp | cornstarch | mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 tsp | szechuan peppercorns | toasted and ground
steps: Slide the tofu into a pot of just-simmering salted water for 2 minutes, then drain gently. This firms it so it holds together.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the pork until browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the chili paste, chili oil, garlic and ginger and fry for a minute until the oil turns red.
Add the stock, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a simmer. Slide in the tofu and simmer for 5 minutes, nudging it gently.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture in two goes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Top with ground Sichuan pepper and scallions.

title: Chicken chow mein
description: Egg noodles stir-fried with chicken, cabbage, carrots and bean sprouts in a savoury soy sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles for a minute less than the packet says, rinse under cold water and drain well. Toss with a little oil.
Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and soy sauce. Mix the sauce.
Heat a wok until very hot with a tablespoon of oil and stir-fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes. Lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic, cabbage and carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes, then the chicken, bean sprouts and scallions for 1 more minute.

title: Chicken pad thai
description: Rice noodles with chicken, egg, bean sprouts and peanuts in a sweet, sour, salty tamarind sauce.
notes: Check your fish sauce and sriracha if you need it gluten free.
steps: Soak the noodles in hot tap water for 20 minutes, until soft but still firm. Drain.
Warm the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar and sriracha, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 3 minutes, then add the garlic and shallot for 30 seconds.
Push everything aside, crack in the eggs and scramble them until nearly set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes until the noodles soak it up. Splash in water if they stick.
Toss in the bean sprouts and scallions, then serve with peanuts, lime and cilantro.

title: Thai green curry with chicken
description: Chicken and vegetables in a fragrant green curry and coconut milk sauce with Thai basil. Serve with jasmine rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a pot with the curry paste and a few spoons of the thick coconut cream from the top of the can. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and the oil splits.
Add the chicken and stir to coat for 2 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the stock and lime leaves and bring to a simmer.
Add the eggplant and cook for 8 minutes, then the pepper and beans for 4 more.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, taste, and stir in the basil just before serving.

title: Red curry with tofu and vegetables
description: Crisp tofu and a pile of vegetables in a red curry coconut sauce. Vegetarian, with soy sauce standing in for fish sauce.
notes: Many red curry pastes contain shrimp; check the label for a vegetarian one.
ingredients: 400 g | firm tofu | pressed and cubed
300 g | sweet potatoes | peeled and cubed
steps: Toss the tofu with the cornstarch. Fry it in the oil in a pan until golden on all sides, then set aside.
Fry the curry paste in the same pan for 2 minutes. Add the coconut milk and stock and bring to a simmer.
Add the sweet potato and simmer for 10 minutes, then the broccoli and pepper for 4 more.
Season with soy sauce, sugar and lime, return the tofu, and add the basil.

title: Thai basil chicken (pad kra pao)
description: Minced chicken stir-fried with garlic, chilies and holy basil, over rice with a crispy fried egg. Thailand's favourite quick lunch.
steps: Pound the garlic and chilies together roughly in a mortar (or chop them finely).
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic and chili for 15 seconds.
Add the chicken and break it up; stir-fry until cooked and lightly browned, about 4 minutes.
Add the sauces, sugar and water and toss until glossy. Turn off the heat and fold in the basil.
Fry the eggs in hot oil until the edges are crisp and lacy. Serve on rice with the chicken.

title: Bibimbap
description: A bowl of rice topped with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg and gochujang sauce, mixed together at the table.
steps: Mix the sauce ingredients.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds and the bean sprouts for 2 minutes. Squeeze the spinach dry. Season each with a little sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry the carrots, zucchini and mushrooms separately in a little oil for 2 minutes each, seasoning each with a pinch of salt.
Fry the beef with the soy sauce, sugar and garlic until browned. Finish with sesame oil.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Put rice in each bowl, arrange the vegetables and beef on top in sections, add an egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and serve with the sauce to mix in.

title: Kimchi fried rice
description: Sour, spicy, deeply savoury rice made with well-fermented kimchi, topped with a runny egg.
ingredients: 200 g | kimchi | chopped, plus 3 tbsp of its juice
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the scallion whites for 30 seconds, then the kimchi for 3 minutes until it starts to caramelise.
Stir in the gochujang and kimchi juice, then the rice. Fry, pressing it into the pan, for 4 minutes until hot and a little crisp.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Fry the eggs and put one on each plate of rice. Finish with scallion greens, sesame and nori.

title: Beef bulgogi
description: Thin slices of beef marinated in soy, pear, garlic and sesame, then seared in a very hot pan until caramelised.
notes: Freeze the beef for 30 minutes first and it's much easier to slice thinly.
steps: Mix the pear, soy sauce, sugar, honey, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and pepper. Add the beef, onion and scallions and marinate for at least 30 minutes (up to overnight).
Heat a large pan or griddle until very hot with a little oil.
Cook the beef in batches in a single layer for 2 to 3 minutes, without moving it at first, until caramelised at the edges.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve with rice, lettuce leaves for wrapping and kimchi.

title: Chicken teriyaki
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs glazed in a homemade soy, mirin and sake sauce. Far better than bottled.
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season it lightly with salt. Mix the sauce ingredients.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and lay the chicken in skin side down. Press it flat and cook for 7 to 8 minutes until the skin is deep golden.
Turn it over and cook for 4 minutes more.
Wipe out most of the fat, pour in the sauce and let it bubble, turning the chicken, until the sauce is thick and glossy, about 3 minutes.
Slice, spoon the glaze over, and top with sesame seeds and scallions.

title: Miso soup with tofu and wakame
description: A clean, savoury bowl of dashi, miso, silken tofu and seaweed, the way it's served with a Japanese breakfast or dinner.
notes: Dashi powder is made from fish. For a vegetarian soup, soak a piece of kombu in the water for 30 minutes instead.
ingredients: 200 g | tofu | silken, in small cubes
steps: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Bring the water to a simmer and stir in the dashi powder.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm through for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat off. Loosen the miso with a ladle of the broth, then stir it back in. Don't boil miso once it's in.
Serve with scallions.

title: Oyakodon (chicken and egg rice bowl)
description: Chicken and onion simmered in sweet dashi and soy, with softly set egg, over rice. The name means parent and child.
ingredients: 300 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in small pieces
steps: Bring the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a simmer in a small frying pan.
Add the onion and simmer for 3 minutes, then the chicken for 6 minutes until cooked.
Pour the eggs over in a circle, cover and cook on low heat for 1 minute, until just set but still soft.
Slide it over bowls of hot rice with some of the broth, and scatter over scallions.

title: Shrimp summer rolls
description: Fresh rice-paper rolls with shrimp, vermicelli, herbs and crunchy vegetables, with a peanut-hoisin dipping sauce.
notes: Hoisin usually contains wheat: use a gluten-free one if you need it.
ingredients: 300 g | shrimp | cooked, peeled, halved lengthwise
steps: Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the sauce ingredients until smooth.
Dip a rice paper in warm water for 5 seconds and lay it on a damp board; it softens as you work.
Lay three shrimp halves pink side down in the middle, then a little lettuce, noodles, carrot, cucumber and herbs on top.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom. Keep the finished rolls under a damp towel.
Serve with the dipping sauce.

title: Garlic sesame noodles
description: Noodles tossed in sizzling garlic-chili oil, soy, black vinegar and sesame paste. Ten minutes from craving to bowl.
steps: Cook the noodles as the packet says. Keep a mug of the cooking water.
In a large bowl, put the garlic, chili flakes, sesame seeds and scallion whites.
Heat the oil until shimmering and pour it over them: it will sizzle hard.
Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, tahini, sugar and sesame oil.
Add the drained noodles and toss, loosening with a splash of noodle water. Top with scallion greens.

title: Crispy tofu and vegetable stir fry
description: Cornstarch-crusted tofu fried crisp, then tossed with vegetables in a sticky garlic-ginger soy glaze.
ingredients: 450 g | firm tofu | pressed and cubed
steps: Toss the tofu with the cornstarch. Fry it in 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat, turning, for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp. Set aside.
Mix the sauce.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then the broccoli and pepper for 3 minutes and the snow peas for 1.
Pour in the sauce and bubble until glossy. Toss in the tofu and serve with rice.

title: Chicken adobo
description: The Philippines' national dish: chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and black pepper until tender and glossy.
ingredients: 1 kg | chicken thighs | bone-in, skin on
steps: Combine everything except the oil in a pot and marinate for 30 minutes if you have time.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and brown it skin side down in the oil in a wide pan. Return it to the pot.
Bring the liquid to a boil without stirring for a few minutes (this mellows the vinegar), then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Uncover and simmer for 10 more minutes, until the sauce reduces and the chicken is tender.
Serve with rice and plenty of the sauce.

title: Nasi goreng
description: Indonesian fried rice with sweet soy, chili and shallots, topped with a fried egg and crunchy cucumber.
notes: Kecap manis is a thick, sweet Indonesian soy sauce. Instead: simmer equal parts soy sauce and brown sugar until syrupy.
steps: Pound or blend the shallots, garlic, chilies and shrimp paste to a rough paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the rice and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes. Add the kecap manis and soy sauce and toss until it's evenly brown.
Fry the eggs. Serve the rice topped with an egg, with cucumber, tomato and scallions.

title: Japanese chicken curry
description: Thick, mild and slightly sweet curry with chicken, potatoes and carrots, made with curry roux blocks. Kids love it.
ingredients: 600 g | chicken thighs | boneless, in chunks
steps: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook until it's no longer pink on the outside.
Add the carrots, potatoes and water. Bring to a boil, skim, and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Turn off the heat and stir in the roux until melted. Add the ketchup, honey and grated apple.
Simmer, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick. Serve over rice.

title: Spaghetti aglio e olio
description: Spaghetti with garlic gently fried in olive oil, chili flakes and parsley. The pantry pasta Italians make at midnight.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | salt | for the pasta water
steps: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Keep a mug of the water.
Meanwhile, put the oil and garlic in a cold pan and heat gently for 4 to 5 minutes until the garlic is pale gold. Don't let it brown, or it turns bitter.
Add the chili flakes, then a ladle of pasta water. It will spit.
Add the drained spaghetti and toss hard for a minute so the oil and water turn into a light sauce. Add more water if it looks dry.
Toss in the parsley, and parmesan if you like.

title: Pasta al pomodoro
description: A simple, sweet tomato sauce with garlic and basil, finished with butter. Proof that three good ingredients are enough.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | salt | for the pasta water
800 g | whole peeled tomatoes | crushed by hand
steps: Warm the oil and garlic in a wide pan over medium heat until the garlic sizzles and turns golden. Take the garlic out.
Add the tomatoes, salt and a few basil leaves. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and sweet.
Meanwhile cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Keep a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta into the sauce with the butter and a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Serve with the rest of the basil and the parmesan.

title: Turkey bolognese
description: A lighter meat sauce with ground turkey, lots of vegetables and a long, slow simmer. Freeze it in portions for easy dinners.
notes: Nutrition is for the sauce only; add your pasta.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrots and celery gently for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for a minute, then turn up the heat and add the turkey. Break it up and cook until it's browned and any liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, oregano, salt and pepper. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Serve with pasta, or cool and freeze in portions.

title: Minestrone
description: A thick Italian vegetable soup with beans and small pasta. Use whatever vegetables are in the fridge.
steps: Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, zucchini and potato for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the beans and pasta and cook for 10 minutes until the pasta is tender. Stir in the kale for the last 3 minutes.
Serve with parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. It thickens overnight; loosen with water.

title: Mushroom risotto
description: Creamy arborio rice stirred with stock, browned mushrooms, white wine and parmesan.
steps: Keep the stock hot in a pan on a low heat.
Brown the mushrooms in the oil over high heat, without stirring too much, for 6 minutes. Season with salt and set aside.
Melt half the butter and cook the shallots and garlic gently for 3 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains turn translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until it's absorbed.
Add a ladle of stock at a time, stirring often and waiting until each is almost absorbed before adding the next, for 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is creamy but still has a little bite.
Stir in the mushrooms, thyme, the rest of the butter and the parmesan. Cover for 2 minutes, then serve.

title: Chicken pesto pasta
description: Pasta, seared chicken, cherry tomatoes and spinach tossed in basil pesto. Good hot or cold from a lunchbox.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | salt | for the pasta water
500 g | chicken breasts | in bite-size pieces
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water. Keep a cup of the water.
Season the chicken and fry it in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 to 7 minutes until golden and cooked.
Add the tomatoes for 2 minutes, then the spinach until it wilts.
Toss in the drained pasta, the pesto and a splash of pasta water until creamy.
Top with parmesan.

title: Baked ziti with spinach
description: Pasta baked in tomato sauce with ricotta, spinach and a bubbling mozzarella top. Make it ahead and bake it when people arrive.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | salt | for the pasta water
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Boil the pasta for 3 minutes less than the packet says and drain.
Mix the ricotta, egg, spinach, half the parmesan, the oregano and pepper.
Toss the pasta with the marinara. Spread half in a baking dish, dot over the ricotta mix, then add the rest of the pasta.
Cover with the mozzarella and remaining parmesan.
Bake for 25 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Caprese salad
description: Ripe tomatoes, fresh mozzarella and basil with good olive oil. Only make it when tomatoes are in season.
steps: Arrange the tomatoes and mozzarella on a plate, overlapping.
Tuck the basil leaves in between.
Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with olive oil (and balsamic if you like) and serve straight away.

title: Chicken burrito bowl
description: Spiced chicken, cilantro-lime rice, black beans, corn, salsa and avocado. A meal-prep favourite: keep the avocado for the day you eat it.
ingredients: 1 can | black beans | drained and rinsed
steps: Rub the chicken with the oil, spices, salt and lime juice. Leave for 15 minutes.
Grill, broil or pan-fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes a side until charred and cooked through. Rest, then slice.
Toss the warm rice with cilantro and lime juice.
Warm the black beans and corn, seasoning with a pinch of salt.
Build the bowls: rice, beans, corn, chicken, salsa, avocado and a spoon of sour cream, with lime wedges.

title: Black bean and sweet potato tacos
description: Roasted chipotle sweet potato and smashed black beans in warm corn tortillas, with pickled onions and feta.
ingredients: 600 g | sweet potatoes | in 1.5 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Toss the sweet potato with the oil, paprika, cumin and half the salt, and roast for 25 minutes until browned.
Warm the beans with the chipotle, the rest of the salt and a splash of water, mashing about half of them.
Char the tortillas one by one over a gas flame or in a dry pan.
Fill with beans and sweet potato, then pickled onions, feta, avocado and cilantro. Squeeze over lime.

title: Chicken fajitas
description: Sizzling strips of chili-lime chicken with peppers and onions, wrapped in warm tortillas at the table.
steps: Toss the chicken with half the oil, the spices, salt and lime juice.
Heat a large cast-iron pan until smoking. Sear the chicken in one layer, in batches, for 3 minutes a side. Lift out.
Add the remaining oil, the peppers and onion and cook over high heat for 5 minutes until charred but still crisp.
Return the chicken and toss. Serve with warm tortillas, sour cream and salsa.

title: Guacamole
description: Chunky avocado mashed with lime, onion, chili and cilantro. Make it just before you eat it.
steps: Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt, leaving it chunky.
Fold in the onion, jalapeño, tomato and cilantro.
Taste for salt and lime. Serve with tortilla chips or on tacos.

title: Huevos rancheros
description: Fried eggs on crisp corn tortillas with a quick cooked salsa, refried beans, avocado and queso fresco.
steps: For the salsa, soften the onion, jalapeño and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes. Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes. Blend briefly if you like it smooth.
Fry the tortillas in a little oil until crisp at the edges, then fry the eggs in the same pan.
Warm the beans.
Spread each tortilla with beans, top with an egg and the salsa, then avocado, queso fresco and cilantro.

title: Chicken and cheese quesadillas
description: Crisp tortillas stuffed with shredded chicken, melting cheese, peppers and a little chipotle. A great use for leftover chicken.
steps: Mix the chicken with the chipotle.
Scatter cheese over half of each tortilla, then chicken, pepper, scallions and a little more cheese. Fold over.
Cook in a dry or lightly buttered pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until crisp and the cheese melts.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa.

title: Turkey and bean chili
description: A hearty, smoky chili with lean turkey, two kinds of beans and plenty of spice. It freezes perfectly.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | chipotles in adobo | optional, chopped
steps: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic for a minute.
Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the spices and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock, salt and chipotle. Simmer, partly covered, for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Serve with rice, cornbread, or cheese and sour cream.

title: Juicy turkey burgers
description: Turkey burgers that don't taste dry: grated onion, Worcestershire and a little mayo keep them moist.
steps: Mix the turkey gently with the onion, garlic, Worcestershire, mayo, paprika, salt and pepper. Don't overwork it.
Shape into 4 patties, a little wider than the buns, with a dimple in the middle so they stay flat.
Cook on a hot oiled grill or pan for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until cooked through (74 °C). Add the cheese for the last minute.
Toast the buns and build the burgers with tomato, lettuce, ketchup and mustard.

title: Sheet-pan chicken with vegetables
description: Chicken thighs, potatoes, broccoli and onions roasted on one tray with garlic, lemon and paprika. One tray to wash.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C.
Toss the potatoes and onion with half the oil and a little of the salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken with the rest of the oil, the garlic, paprika, oregano, salt, pepper and lemon.
Add the chicken and broccoli to the tray and roast for 20 to 25 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked and everything is browned.
Divide into boxes for the week, or serve straight from the tray.

title: Stovetop mac and cheese
description: Creamy, proper cheese sauce from scratch in the time it takes to boil the pasta.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | salt | for the pasta water
steps: Boil the macaroni in salted water until just tender and drain.
Melt the butter in a pan, stir in the flour and cook for a minute.
Whisk in the milk a little at a time, then simmer, whisking, for 3 to 4 minutes until thick.
Take it off the heat and stir in the mustard, cheeses, salt, pepper and nutmeg until smooth.
Stir in the macaroni. Loosen with a splash of milk if needed.

title: Chicken noodle soup
description: The cure-all: poached chicken, carrots, celery and egg noodles in a golden broth with dill.
steps: Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic for a minute.
Add the stock, bay leaves, thyme and salt and bring to a simmer.
Add the whole chicken breasts and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked. Lift them out and shred with two forks.
Add the noodles to the pot and cook for 7 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the lemon juice and dill, and taste for salt.

title: Québec-style split pea soup
description: Thick yellow pea soup with smoky ham, carrots and summer savoury: a Québec winter classic, very cheap and very filling.
notes: Traditionally made with dried summer savoury; use it instead of the thyme if you have it.
steps: Put everything except the salt in a large pot and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam.
Simmer, partly covered, for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch, until the peas have broken down.
Take out the bay leaves. Mash some of the soup, or blend a third of it, for a thicker texture.
Season with salt at the end (the ham is salty) and loosen with water if it's too thick.

title: Maple-soy glazed salmon
description: Salmon fillets roasted with a sticky glaze of maple syrup, soy sauce, garlic and ginger.
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C and line a tray with baking paper.
Whisk the maple syrup, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, mustard and pepper.
Lay the salmon on the tray and spoon over half the glaze.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes until it just flakes. Brush with the rest of the glaze for the last 2 minutes.
Top with sesame seeds and scallions.

title: Crunchy coleslaw
description: Crisp cabbage and carrot in a light, tangy yogurt-mayo dressing. It goes with every barbecue.
steps: Toss the cabbages, carrots and scallions in a big bowl.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yogurt, vinegar, mustard, honey, salt and pepper.
Toss the dressing through the vegetables. Leave for 10 minutes before serving so it softens a little.

title: High-protein tuna salad
description: Canned tuna with Greek yogurt, celery, pickles and lemon: for sandwiches, wraps, crackers or lettuce cups.
notes: A can here is about 140 g drained.
steps: Flake the tuna into a bowl.
Stir in everything else.
Taste for salt and lemon. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Fluffy pancakes
description: Thick, soft buttermilk-style pancakes made with ordinary milk and a squeeze of lemon.
ingredients: 1 tbsp | neutral oil | for the pan
steps: Stir the lemon juice into the milk and leave for 5 minutes: it will thicken a little.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg, melted butter and vanilla into the milk, then pour it into the flour and stir just until combined. Lumps are fine; overmixing makes them tough.
Heat a lightly oiled pan over medium heat. Pour in 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and cook until bubbles cover the top, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
Serve with maple syrup.

title: Protein overnight oats
description: Oats soaked overnight in milk and Greek yogurt with chia and berries. Make five jars on Sunday.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia, maple syrup and cinnamon together in a jar.
Top with the berries, close the lid and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
Eat cold, or warm it for a minute in the microwave. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Masala omelette
description: A thin Indian omelette with onion, tomato, green chili and cilantro. Eat it with toast, or fold it into a roti.
steps: Beat the eggs with everything except the butter.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and pour in the eggs, swirling to spread them.
Cook for 2 minutes until the base is golden, then flip (or fold) and cook for 30 seconds more.

title: Veggie egg muffins
description: Baked egg cups with spinach, peppers and feta. Reheat two for a grab-and-go breakfast all week.
ingredients: 1 tsp | neutral oil | for the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and oil a 12-hole muffin tin well.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Divide the vegetables and feta among the holes, then pour over the egg.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until puffed and set in the middle.
Cool for 5 minutes before lifting out. Keep 4 days in the fridge; reheat for 30 seconds.

title: Greek yogurt parfait
description: Thick yogurt layered with berries, honey, nuts and a handful of oats.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden (or skip it).
Layer the yogurt, fruit, oats and almonds in a glass.
Drizzle with honey.

title: Avocado toast with egg
description: Crushed avocado with lemon and chili flakes on toasted sourdough, topped with a jammy egg.
steps: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel. (Or fry them.)
Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Spread it on the toast, halve the eggs on top, drizzle with oil and finish with salt and chili flakes.

title: Peanut butter banana smoothie
description: A thick, filling smoothie of banana, peanut butter, oats, milk and Greek yogurt. Breakfast in a glass.
notes: Use certified gluten-free oats if you need it gluten free.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and creamy.
Add a splash more milk if it's too thick.

title: Apple cinnamon oatmeal
description: Creamy oats cooked with milk, grated apple and cinnamon, topped with walnuts and maple syrup.
steps: Put the oats, milk, water, apple, cinnamon and salt in a pan.
Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring, for 5 to 7 minutes until thick and creamy.
Serve with walnuts and a drizzle of maple syrup.

title: Smooth hummus
description: Silky hummus with plenty of tahini and lemon. The trick is blending the chickpeas warm, with ice water.
steps: Blend the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and cumin for a minute until thick and pale.
Add the warm chickpeas and blend for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides.
With the motor running, pour in the ice water a little at a time until the hummus is very smooth and fluffy.
Spread it in a bowl, make a swirl with the back of a spoon, and fill it with olive oil and a pinch of paprika.

title: Baked falafel
description: Herby falafel made from soaked (not canned) chickpeas and baked until crisp. Stuff them into pita with salad and tahini.
ingredients: 250 g | dried chickpeas | soaked overnight, drained and dried
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C and oil a baking tray with a tablespoon of the oil.
Pulse the chickpeas, onion, garlic and herbs in a food processor until finely chopped, like coarse sand. Don't make a paste.
Mix in the spices, salt, baking soda and chickpea flour. Chill for 15 minutes.
Shape into 20 small patties and put them on the tray. Brush with the rest of the oil.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. Bring the pan to the table with bread for dipping.
steps: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and spices for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, salt and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Make six hollows in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Scatter with feta and parsley.

title: Chicken shawarma
description: Chicken thighs marinated in yogurt, lemon, garlic and warm spices, roasted hot and sliced. Serve in pita, on rice or over salad.
steps: Mix everything except the chicken and onion, then coat the chicken. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Heat the oven to 230 °C. Spread the chicken and onion on a lined tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until charred at the edges. Switch to the grill for the last 3 minutes for more colour.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly. Serve with pita, tahini sauce, pickles and salad.

title: Tabbouleh
description: A bright green parsley salad with a little bulgur, tomato, mint and lemon. Mostly herbs, the Lebanese way.
steps: Rinse the bulgur and soak it in the lemon juice for 15 minutes until tender.
Chop the herbs very finely with a sharp knife (a food processor bruises them).
Mix the bulgur, herbs, tomatoes and scallions.
Dress with the olive oil, salt and allspice. Serve soon, with lettuce leaves to scoop.

title: Mujadara (lentils and rice with crispy onions)
description: Lentils and rice cooked with cumin and topped with a pile of deeply browned onions. Humble, cheap and very good.
steps: Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat with a pinch of salt, stirring often, for 25 to 30 minutes until dark brown and crisp. Lift half out onto paper.
Meanwhile, simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes until half cooked, then drain.
Add the rice, cumin and cinnamon to the onions left in the pot and stir for a minute. Add the lentils, water and salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 18 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff it up, top with the crispy onions and serve with yogurt.

title: Turkish red lentil soup (mercimek çorbası)
description: Smooth, golden soup of red lentils, carrot and onion with mint and chili butter on top. Squeeze in plenty of lemon.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and potato in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika for a minute.
Add the lentils, stock and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes until everything is soft.
Blend until smooth. Add water if it's too thick.
Melt the butter until foaming, take it off the heat and stir in the mint and chili flakes. Drizzle over each bowl and serve with lemon.

title: Baba ganoush
description: Smoky roasted eggplant mashed with tahini, garlic and lemon.
steps: Char the eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill, turning, for 15 to 20 minutes until collapsed and blackened all over.
Leave them in a bowl, covered, for 10 minutes. Then peel off the skin and drain the flesh in a sieve for 10 minutes.
Mash the flesh with a fork, then stir in the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
Spread in a bowl and top with olive oil, parsley and pomegranate.

title: Chicken souvlaki with tzatziki
description: Lemon, garlic and oregano chicken skewers, grilled and served with cool cucumber tzatziki.
ingredients: 800 g | chicken breasts | in 3 cm cubes
steps: Mix the oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper and toss the chicken in it. Marinate for 30 minutes to 4 hours.
Stir together the tzatziki ingredients and chill.
Thread the chicken onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water first).
Grill over high heat or on a griddle pan for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with tzatziki, pita, tomatoes and onion.

title: Greek salad
description: Tomatoes, cucumber, peppers, red onion, olives and a slab of feta with oregano and olive oil. No lettuce.
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion and olives in a wide bowl. Season with salt and toss with the vinegar.
Lay the feta on top.
Sprinkle with oregano and pour over the olive oil. Serve with bread to mop up the juices.

title: Greek lemon chicken and potatoes
description: Chicken thighs and potatoes roasted in lemon, garlic, oregano and stock until the potatoes soak it all up.
ingredients: 1 kg | chicken thighs | bone-in, skin on
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Toss the potatoes and chicken in it.
Spread the potatoes in a roasting tin, sit the chicken on top skin side up, and pour the stock around the potatoes.
Roast for 55 to 60 minutes, until the chicken skin is crisp and the potatoes are tender and golden at the edges. Baste once halfway.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the pan juices and a salad.

title: Beef kofta
description: Spiced beef and herb skewers, grilled until charred. Serve with hummus, salad and flatbread.
steps: Mix everything except the oil with your hands for a minute, until it's slightly sticky.
Shape into 12 sausages around skewers, or just as patties. Chill for 15 minutes.
Brush with oil and grill or pan-fry over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.

title: Roasted tomato soup
description: Tomatoes, onion and garlic roasted until sweet, then blended with stock and a little cream. Made for grilled cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Toss the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the oil, salt and pepper on a tray.
Roast for 35 minutes until soft and charred at the edges.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins into a pot with everything from the tray and the stock. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and basil, and taste for salt.

title: Butternut squash soup
description: Velvety roasted squash soup with ginger, a little maple and coconut milk. Autumn in a bowl.
ingredients: 1.2 kg | butternut squash | peeled and cubed
steps: Heat the oven to 210 °C. Toss the squash with half the oil and roast for 25 minutes until soft and browned.
Meanwhile soften the onion in the rest of the oil for 8 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for a minute.
Add the squash, stock, maple syrup, salt and nutmeg and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until silky, then stir in the coconut milk. Serve with toasted pepitas.

title: Lighter chicken Caesar salad
description: Crisp romaine, sliced chicken and crunchy croutons with a punchy yogurt Caesar dressing: all the flavour, less of the oil.
steps: Whisk the dressing ingredients until smooth. Thin with a spoon of water if needed.
Toss the lettuce with most of the dressing.
Top with the chicken, croutons and parmesan and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.

title: Quinoa chickpea salad
description: Quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, herbs and feta in lemon vinaigrette. It keeps well for lunches.
steps: Simmer the quinoa in the water, covered, for 15 minutes until the water is gone. Rest for 5 minutes, fluff and cool.
Mix the quinoa with the chickpeas, vegetables and herbs.
Toss with the vinaigrette and salt, then fold in the feta. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Crispy roasted chickpeas
description: Crunchy, spiced chickpeas from the oven: a cheap, high-fibre snack.
ingredients: 480 g | cooked chickpeas | patted very dry
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Rub the chickpeas in a towel to dry them and remove loose skins.
Toss with the oil and roast on a tray for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp.
Toss with the spices and salt while hot. They soften after a day, so eat them soon.

title: Date and nut energy balls
description: Dates, oats, nuts and cocoa rolled into bite-size balls. No baking, no added sugar.
steps: Blend the oats and almonds to a coarse meal.
Add the dates, peanut butter, cocoa, chia and salt and blend until it clumps together. Add a spoon of water if it's dry.
Roll into 16 balls. Keep in the fridge for a week.

title: Masala peanuts
description: Peanuts in a crunchy, spicy chickpea-flour coating, baked instead of fried. Dangerous with a cup of chai.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Mix the peanuts with the flours, spices, salt and oil. Sprinkle in the water a spoon at a time, tossing, until every peanut has a thin coat.
Spread on a lined tray, separating the peanuts, and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring once, until crisp.
Cool completely: they crisp up more as they cool.

title: Banana bread
description: Moist, deeply banana-flavoured loaf. The riper and blacker the bananas, the better.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C and line a loaf tin.
Mix the bananas, butter, sugar, egg and vanilla in a bowl.
Sprinkle over the baking soda, salt and cinnamon and stir, then fold in the flour and walnuts until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack.

title: Chewy chocolate chip cookies
description: Crisp at the edges, chewy in the middle, with melted butter and chopped dark chocolate.
steps: Whisk the butter and both sugars until glossy, then whisk in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt, then the chocolate.
Chill the dough for 30 minutes (or up to 3 days). Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Roll into 18 balls, space them well apart on lined trays and bake for 10 to 11 minutes, until golden at the edges but soft in the middle.
Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before moving them.

title: Coconut mango chia pudding
description: Chia seeds set overnight in coconut milk, topped with fresh mango. Dessert or breakfast.
steps: Whisk the chia seeds, coconut milk, water, maple syrup, vanilla and salt.
Leave for 10 minutes, whisk again to break up clumps, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Spoon into glasses and top with mango.

title: Carrot halwa (gajar ka halwa)
description: Grated carrots slowly cooked in milk with ghee, sugar and cardamom until rich and jammy. The winter sweet of North India.
steps: Cook the carrots in the milk in a heavy pan over medium heat, stirring often, for 35 to 40 minutes until the milk has almost gone.
Add the ghee and sugar and keep stirring for 10 minutes. The sugar will loosen it, then it thickens again and turns glossy.
Stir in the cardamom, cashews and raisins.
Serve warm, topped with pistachios.

title: Mango sticky rice
description: Sweet, salty coconut glutinous rice with ripe mango and a drizzle of coconut sauce.
ingredients: 200 g | glutinous rice | soaked at least 2 hours
steps: Drain the rice and steam it in a cloth-lined steamer for 20 to 25 minutes until tender and translucent.
Meanwhile warm 200 ml of the coconut milk with the sugar and half the salt until dissolved.
Stir the hot rice into the sweet coconut milk, cover and leave for 20 minutes to soak it up.
Warm the rest of the coconut milk with the remaining salt for the sauce.
Serve the rice with mango, a spoon of sauce and sesame seeds.

title: Nimbu pani (spiced lemonade)
description: Fresh lemonade with a pinch of salt, roasted cumin and black pepper. Salty-sweet and very refreshing.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp | cumin seeds | toasted and ground
steps: Stir the sugar and salt into a little of the water until dissolved.
Add the lemon juice, the rest of the water, the cumin and pepper.
Pour over ice with mint leaves.

title: Honey iced latte
description: Strong coffee over ice with cold milk and a spoon of honey. Cheaper than the café.
steps: Stir the honey into the warm coffee until it dissolves, then let it cool.
Fill a glass with ice, pour in the milk, then the coffee.

title: Golden milk (haldi doodh)
description: Warm milk with turmeric, ginger, black pepper and a little honey. A bedtime drink for a cold night.
steps: Warm the milk with the turmeric, ginger, pepper and cinnamon until it just simmers.
Leave it on low heat for 5 minutes, then strain.
Stir in the honey off the heat.
